newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GBL's de Rudder named independent SGB board member.
newsitem.headline: GBL's de Rudder named independent SGB board member.

text.p: Shareholders of Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) have approved the appointment of Thierry de Rudder, a director of holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL), as an SGB board member.
De Rudder will take his seat as independent board member.
"I will fulfil this mandate as any other mandate, in the interest of all shareholders of the company," de Rudder told Reuters after SGB's annual shareholders meeting.
It will be the first time that SBG, the largest and oldest holding company in Belgium, has taken a representative of its main competitor onto its board of directors.

At the shareholders meeting, SGB Chairman Etienne Davignon told shareholders that the issue of having a GBL representative on the board has been around for a long time as GBL controls about two percent of SGB's capital, making it SGB's third most important shareholder.
GBL holds the stake via its unit Compagnie Nationale a Portefeuille (CNP).

Asked whether de Rudder's nomination was due to the fact that GBL had now become an important minority shareholder in SGB parent Compagnie de Suez, Davignon said: "That is not the reason, but it doesn't prevent it either."

De Rudder told Reuters that his appointment in itself would not resolve hot issues between the two groups, notably the long-time plan to merge SGB unit Generale Bank with GBL unit Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL).
Davignon reiterated earlier today that the idea of a merger remains blocked by opposition from Dutch BBL minority shareholders Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING).
SGB shareholders also approved the nomination of Christine Morin-Postel, a representative of Suez, as board member.
